functional.statement: WHEN a sponsor org begins onboarding, the system SHALL provide a Company (CO) template form that captures sponsor details and emits a conformant REP CO XML file whose template-generated filename (pattern final-com-<COMPANYID>-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<HHMM>.xml) is preserved verbatim and never editable by any user, treating the HC-assigned Company ID as an opaque token rather than hardcoding a 5-digit numeric format.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a completed CO form WHEN the user generates the CO XML THEN the system produces a 'final-' prefixed XML file and records the returned HC-assigned Company ID against the org
GIVEN a returned Company ID WHEN stored THEN the system validates it loosely as an HC-assigned opaque token (alphanumeric permitted, e.g. K18276) and does NOT reject non-5-digit values
GIVEN a generated REP CO XML WHEN any user attempts to rename or change its extension THEN the system blocks the action and warns that REP filenames are immutable
GIVEN a CO form WHEN the user adds a contact and saves THEN the system stores the contact and its HC-issued contact ID for reference by later transactions
functional.rationale: REP CO is the mandatory front-door identifier acquisition; HC-generated immutable filenames must be carried verbatim or the transaction is rejected. The only concrete sample token (final-com-K18276-...) is 6-char alphanumeric, so a 5-digit-numeric validator would reject HC's own IDs.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH REP topic: 'FILE NAMING IS MACHINE-GENERATED AND IMMUTABLE'; CORRECTION 'Company ID format unverified/too strict'; VISION Onboarding & Enrolment Wizard

functional.statement: WHEN a user needs a Dossier ID for a transaction, the system SHALL provide a product-type-and-activity-branched workflow (pharmaceutical/biologic, pharmaceutical clinical-trial, biologic clinical-trial, veterinary, biocide, medical device, and Master File) that either (a) requests a NEW Dossier ID and warns when the request is placed MORE than 8 weeks before the intended first-filing date, or (b) reuses an EXISTING Dossier ID for continuing sequences in the same format (no new request), with an optional DSTS-IA lookup, and tracks request status until any HC-assigned ID is returned.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a Dossier ID request WHEN the user selects a product type/activity THEN the system presents the corresponding HC request form fields and lead-time guidance, including the clinical-trial and Master File branches

GIVEN a NEW Dossier ID request placed MORE than 8 weeks before the intended first-filing date WHEN submitted THEN the system warns the request is too early (HC's 8-week MAXIMUM lead time), and does NOT gate or flag requests placed within 8 weeks

GIVEN a continuing sequence on an existing dossier in the same format WHEN created THEN the system skips the request and reuses the stored Dossier ID, optionally offering a DSTS-IA lookup (client.information@hc-sc.gc.ca)

GIVEN a returned drug Dossier ID WHEN entered THEN the system validates it against a prefix-by-type pattern (default ANDS prefix 'e', ^[a-z][0-9]{6,7}$; e=pharma/biologic & eCTD Master Files, f+7=non-eCTD Master Files, m=medical device) and rejects non-conforming values
GIVEN a referenced DMF/Master File WHEN cited THEN the system requires its own e+6 (eCTD) or f+7 (non-eCTD) Dossier ID requested on its own form
functional.rationale: A valid Dossier ID is a hard prerequisite to assembling any transaction. The 'm' prefix is the medical-device convention; ANDS pharmaceutical/biologic eCTD IDs use 'e' with 6 or 7 digits by activity type. HC's 8-week rule is a MAXIMUM (don't request too early), not a minimum lead-time gate; and most ANDS work is follow-up sequences that reuse an existing dossier.
functional.traces_to: CORRECTION 'Dossier ID format' (e prefix, 6/7 digits) + 'Dossier ID 8-week rule direction' (maximum, warn when too early); GAP existing-dossier/DSTS-IA path; GAP dossier-ID request branches (clinical-trial, Master File); VISION Onboarding & Enrolment Wizard

functional.statement: WHEN a sponsor configures transmission, the system SHALL target FDA ESG NextGen (deployed April 2025) and capture FDA ESG account setup (WebTrader or AS2/EDIINT), allow X.509 certificate upload, designate 'HC' as the recipient Center, and require a successful Test-gateway round-trip (acknowledgements received) before any Production transmission is permitted, pinning the targeted ESG environment version as tracked configuration.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN no completed Test-gateway round-trip WHEN a user attempts a Production transmission THEN the system blocks it and directs the user to complete the test checklist
GIVEN ESG setup WHEN the user selects AS2 vs WebTrader THEN the system stores the account type, the X.509 certificate, and required NextGen registration config as first-class data

GIVEN a transmission configuration WHEN saved THEN the recipient Center is set to 'HC', the targeted ESG environment is pinned to FDA ESG NextGen, and the system never targets a direct Health Canada AS2 endpoint
functional.rationale: CESG rides on the FDA ESG (no direct HC endpoint); a successful test round-trip is mandated before production. The integration must target FDA ESG NextGen (April 2025) registration portal, API surface and ACK model, and pin the environment version the way the validation ruleset is pinned.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH CESG topic ONBOARDING; CORRECTION 'FDA ESG NextGen context missing'; GAP target FDA ESG NextGen; VISION health_canada_integration

functional.statement: WHEN a new submission is created, the system SHALL present a submission-type router (NDS/ANDS/SNDS/SANDS/DIN) with decision support and, when ANDS is selected, configure the ANDS content model so Module 4 is marked not-required, Module 3 (CMC) and Module 5 BE reports are required, and the CS-BE (BE-only) path suppresses Modules 2.4-2.7 while keeping the 2.3 QOS required.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN ANDS is selected WHEN the content model is configured THEN Module 4 is shown as not-required and Module 3 (CMC) and Module 5 BE reports are shown as required
GIVEN the CS-BE (BE-only) path is toggled on WHEN the tree is rendered THEN Modules 2.4-2.7 are suppressed (including 2.7.1) and the 2.3 QOS remains required
GIVEN a dossier that also contains other safety/efficacy studies WHEN the content model is configured THEN Modules 2.4-2.7 are completed as applicable (the non-CS-BE-only path)
GIVEN a generic seeking a new indication beyond the CRP WHEN routing THEN the system advises that ANDS is generally not the correct pathway
functional.rationale: ANDS-native module gating prevents wrong-module effort and missing-content rejections. The CS-BE path's whole point is that 2.4-2.7 (including 2.7.1) are suppressed; emitting a 2.7.1 while suppressing 2.4-2.7 is non-conformant.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH ANDS topic: Module 4 not required, CS-BE replaces 2.4-2.7; CORRECTION 'CS-BE placement & 2.7.1 contradiction'; VISION New Submission Intake & Type Router

functional.statement: WHEN an ANDS submission is configured, the system SHALL resolve the regulatory activity type from HC's published Module 1 controlled vocabulary that includes ANDS and feed it into the REP RT template, rejecting any value not in HC's controlled vocabulary.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN activity-type selection WHEN the user picks a value THEN only HC controlled-vocabulary values (ingested from HC's published CV files) are selectable
GIVEN a resolved activity type WHEN an RT template is generated THEN the activity type and regulatory activity lead populate the RT XML
GIVEN a metadata value not in the controlled vocabulary WHEN validation runs THEN the system raises an Error mirroring rule I08
functional.rationale: Activity/enumeration values not in HC controlled vocabulary cause rejection (I08); RT must accompany every transaction.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic rule I08; REP topic RT template; GAP HC-published CV/enumeration files; VISION New Submission Intake & Type Router

functional.statement: The system SHALL generate a Regulatory Transaction (RT) template XML (current version v5.1.0, 2025-09-10) for every regulatory transaction, and a Product Information (PI) template (current version 2024-02-12) where the transaction subset requires it, preserving template-generated immutable filenames and placing the REP transaction metadata for a drug ANDS in m1/ca/ca-regional.xml; the Application Information (AI) template and the 1.04/1.05 folder placement are MEDICAL-DEVICE/IMDRF-only and SHALL NOT be applied to the drug ANDS path.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN any drug ANDS transaction WHEN it is assembled THEN an RT XML (v5.1.0+) is generated and its metadata lands in m1/ca/ca-regional.xml (CA Module 1 Schema v2.2), not in a device 1.04 folder
GIVEN a transaction subset requiring PI WHEN assembled THEN a PI template XML (2024-02-12) is also generated; otherwise PI is omitted
GIVEN generated RT/PI XML WHEN packaged THEN their HC-template filenames are carried verbatim
GIVEN a drug ANDS WHEN assembled THEN the AI template and the 1.04/1.05 placement are NOT used (device/IMDRF path only)
functional.rationale: RT is mandatory with every transaction and PI for a subset; both must be conformant and immutably named. The AI template and 1.04/1.05 placement are device/IMDRF ToC, not drug eCTD; for an ANDS the REP metadata belongs in m1/ca/ca-regional.xml. Template versions jumped to the 5.x generation in 2025.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH REP topic; CORRECTION 'AI template / 1.04 placement scoped to drugs'; CORRECTION 'REP template versions stale'; VISION REP integration feature

functional.statement: WHEN capturing the Canadian Reference Product, the system SHALL require structured CRP fields (brand name, DIN, strength, dosage form, innovator/manufacturer) and provide a foreign-CRP justification path, validating that the proposed generic is pharmaceutically equivalent (identical medicinal ingredient(s) in comparable dosage form).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a CRP entry WHEN required fields are missing THEN the system blocks progression and lists the missing fields
GIVEN a proposed generic and CRP WHEN medicinal ingredient or dosage-form comparability fails THEN the system flags a pharmaceutical-equivalence defect
GIVEN a foreign-sourced reference product WHEN selected THEN the system requires a justification record per the foreign-CRP path
functional.rationale: The CRP and pharmaceutical equivalence are the legal heart of an ANDS (C.08.001.1 / C.08.002.1).
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH ANDS topic: CRP definition, pharmaceutical equivalence; VISION CRP & Bioequivalence Builder

functional.statement: WHEN building bioequivalence evidence for a BE-only ANDS, the system SHALL provide a CS-BE builder that places the CS-BE electronic copy in Module 1.6, links full pivotal study reports into Module 5.3.1.2, and does NOT generate a Module 2.7.1 (2.4-2.7 suppressed); it SHALL capture AUC and Cmax results and branch Cmax acceptance by the applicable BE ruleset version: point-estimate (relative mean) within 80.0-125.0% for legacy/pre-ICH-M13A or non-IR products, versus the full 90% confidence interval within 80.00-125.00% under ICH M13A (effective 2025-12-27, IR solid oral). The CS-BE path SHALL carry a draft-status flag (CS-BE template and comparative-BA CTD guidance are DRAFT, dated 2004-05-18).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a completed CS-BE for a BE-only ANDS WHEN saved THEN its electronic copy is placed in Module 1.6, full study reports are linked into Module 5.3.1.2, and NO 2.7.1 is generated
GIVEN entered AUC 90% CI bounds WHEN they fall outside 80.0-125.0% (or 80.00-125.00% under M13A) THEN the system flags a bioequivalence acceptance-limit failure
GIVEN a pre-M13A or non-IR product WHEN Cmax is validated THEN the system checks the Cmax POINT ESTIMATE within 80.0-125.0% and does not require a 90% CI for Cmax
GIVEN an IR solid-oral product filed on/after 2025-12-27 WHEN Cmax is validated THEN the system requires the full Cmax 90% CI within 80.00-125.00% per ICH M13A
GIVEN the CS-BE path WHEN presented THEN it is labelled as based on DRAFT guidance and the system can adapt when the CS-BE/comparative-BA guidance is finalized
functional.rationale: The CS-BE electronic copy is filed in Module 1.6 with full reports in 5.3.1.2; emitting a 2.7.1 while suppressing 2.4-2.7 is contradictory. The Cmax acceptance rule is a versioned moving target (point-estimate pre-M13A vs full 90% CI under M13A); both CS-BE and the comparative-BA CTD guidance remain DRAFT.
functional.traces_to: CORRECTION 'CS-BE placement & 2.7.1 contradiction'; CORRECTION 'Cmax acceptance criterion versioned'; CORRECTION 'draft-status of CS-BE'; GAP CS-BE in Module 1.6; GAP M13A version branch; VISION CRP & Bioequivalence Builder

functional.statement: The system SHALL drive the eCTD tree and Module 1 leaf placement from Health Canada's 'Organization and document placement' heading table (updated 2024-04-02) as versioned data, including required .docx-alongside-PDF documents where specified; the cover letter is sponsor-AUTHORED and placed under the m1-0-1-cover-letter leaf (heading 1.0) — HC provides only the placement slot, not a fillable cover-letter template.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN the document-placement table WHEN the tree is rendered THEN each CA Module 1 heading maps to its prescribed leaf location, including the m1-0-1-cover-letter slot under heading 1.0
GIVEN a section that requires a .docx alongside the PDF WHEN the checklist renders THEN both formats are required for that section
GIVEN a cover letter WHEN authored THEN it is generated from the portal's OWN template (no HC cover-letter .docx is expected) and placed in the cover-letter slot
GIVEN an updated placement table WHEN loaded THEN placement changes apply without code changes
functional.rationale: Driving placement from HC's heading table as data keeps the portal current. The cover letter is sponsor-authored; HC provides only the placement slot, so engineers must not hunt for a non-existent HC cover-letter form.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic: HC heading reference table; CORRECTION 'cover letter wrongly implied an HC fillable template'; VISION Dossier Workspace / CTD Tree Editor

functional.statement: WHEN documents are uploaded into the workspace, the system SHALL enforce PDF conformance (versions 1.4-1.7, text-based/searchable with OCR for scanned pages, fonts embedded, no encryption/passwords/security settings, no DRM/IRM/restricted-access/rights-management settings, no enabled Track Changes, not corrupt).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an encrypted or password-protected PDF WHEN uploaded THEN the system blocks it with an Error mirroring rule A09
GIVEN a PDF with DRM/IRM/restricted-access or rights-management settings WHEN uploaded THEN the system blocks it (HC explicitly prohibits non-password security settings)
GIVEN a scanned non-searchable PDF WHEN uploaded THEN the system flags it for OCR mirroring rules B49/D29
GIVEN a PDF outside versions 1.4-1.7 or with Track Changes enabled WHEN validated THEN the system raises a conformance defect mapped to the file
functional.rationale: Non-searchable, secured, or corrupt PDFs are common rejection triggers (A09/B49/D29). HC also explicitly blocks DRM/IRM/restricted-access/rights-management beyond simple passwords, which would fail at HC even if the portal's basic encryption check passes.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic PDF rules A09/B49/D29; GAP DRM/IRM/restricted-access prohibition; VISION Dossier Workspace / CTD Tree Editor

functional.statement: WHEN a PDF exceeding 10 pages is uploaded, the system SHALL automatically generate single-action bookmarks (one action per bookmark opening its destination), with the documented exceptions for literature references in 3.3/4.3/5.4 and Health Canada e-forms.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an 11-page content PDF WHEN uploaded THEN the system generates bookmarks and each bookmark has exactly one action
GIVEN a literature reference under 3.3/4.3/5.4 or an HC e-form WHEN uploaded THEN bookmark generation is exempted
GIVEN generated bookmarks WHEN validation runs THEN no broken/multi-action bookmark defects are raised
functional.rationale: Manual bookmarking is one of the most error-prone, time-consuming RA tasks; automating it is a major pass-rate and productivity win.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH tool-landscape topic: bookmarks >10 pages; VISION automated PDF remediation feature

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide intra-document and inter-document hyperlinking that produces functional relative internal links and SHALL reject or flag external/absolute web hyperlinks in content PDFs.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a cross-reference within or between documents WHEN authored THEN the system creates a relative, functional hyperlink
GIVEN an absolute external web hyperlink in a content PDF WHEN validated THEN the system flags it as a defect mapped to the link
GIVEN a broken bookmark or hyperlink WHEN validation runs THEN the defect is surfaced before export
functional.rationale: Broken/external links are flagged by HC validation; automated relative linking removes a major manual error source.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic: relative internal links; VISION automated PDF remediation feature

functional.statement: WHEN a content file approaches or exceeds the per-file size limit, the system SHALL warn at the 150-200 MB band (mirroring A03a) and hard-block any single PDF at or above 200 MB (mirroring A03b), offering an automated oversize-split workflow.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a 170 MB PDF WHEN validated THEN the system issues a non-blocking Warning advising a split (A03a)
GIVEN a 210 MB PDF WHEN validated THEN the system raises a blocking Error and offers to split the file (A03b)
GIVEN a non-PDF file above the configured non-PDF ceiling WHEN validated THEN the system raises the corresponding Error
functional.rationale: A03a (Warn 150-200MB) and A03b (Error >=200MB) are real published HC validation rules, not tool-config; pre-empting and auto-splitting prevents republish cycles.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH CESG topic; CORRECTION '150/200MB tool-config hedge' (real A03a/A03b rules); VISION Pre-Submission Validation Report

functional.statement: The system SHALL deterministically generate both backbones for each sequence — the ICH index.xml (validated against HC's published ICH eCTD v3.2.2 DTD) with index-md5.txt at the sequence root, and the Canadian ca-regional.xml under m1/ca/ generated and validated against the pinned Canadian Module 1 Schema v2.2 XSD (dated 2012-07-06) — plus the util/ folder carrying the exact HC-published ICH eCTD DTD and XSL stylesheet, validating each backbone against its schema/DTD before export.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a sequence WHEN backbones are generated THEN index.xml, index-md5.txt and m1/ca/ca-regional.xml exist, the ca-regional.xml conforms to the pinned Schema v2.2 XSD (root element resolved from the actual XSD, not asserted prose), and util/ carries the HC-published ICH eCTD DTD + XSL
GIVEN a generated backbone WHEN it fails schema/DTD validation THEN the system blocks export with an Error mirroring A06a/H08
GIVEN index.xml WHEN validated THEN it is checked against the ICH eCTD v3.2.2 DTD in util/, not only the regional XSD
GIVEN two backbone generation runs on identical content WHEN compared THEN the output is byte-deterministic
functional.rationale: Backbone/schema errors (A06a, H08) are top rejection triggers; dual-backbone correctness is non-negotiable. The real Schema v2.2 XSD and ICH 3.2.2 DTD must be pinned and generated against (not against element names asserted in prose, which were dossier-inconsistent), and util/ must carry the published DTD/XSL.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic; CORRECTION 'ca-regional.xml root element unverified'; GAP util/ DTD+XSL and validate index.xml against the DTD; VISION dual-backbone generator feature

functional.statement: WHEN a sequence is saved or exported, the system SHALL compute a per-leaf MD5 checksum (checksum-type 'MD5'), record it in the backbone, write index-md5.txt for index.xml, and re-verify every stored checksum against the actual file bytes, hard-blocking on any mismatch.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN leaf files WHEN a sequence is saved THEN each leaf carries a matching MD5 and checksum-type attribute
GIVEN a file altered after checksum computation WHEN re-verification runs THEN the system raises a blocking checksum-mismatch Error
GIVEN index.xml WHEN written THEN index-md5.txt contains its correct MD5 hash
functional.rationale: Checksum mismatch or missing index-md5.txt is an Error and a top rejection trigger; re-verification against bytes is mandatory.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic: MD5 per leaf, index-md5.txt; VISION dual-backbone generator feature

functional.statement: The system SHALL auto-assign 4-digit zero-padded sequence numbers per dossier (initial = 0000, strictly +1 with no gaps and no repeats) and block any transaction that would skip, repeat, or precede a missing predecessor (mirroring A05a/A05b/A07).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a new dossier's first transaction WHEN created THEN the sequence folder is exactly 0000
GIVEN existing sequences 0000 and 0001 WHEN the next is created THEN it is assigned 0002 and no gap is allowed
GIVEN an attempt to file 0004 while 0003 is missing WHEN validated THEN the system blocks with an Error mirroring A05b/A07
functional.rationale: Gapped/out-of-order sequencing (A05/A07) causes rejection; server-side enforcement removes a dominant incumbent failure mode.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH lifecycle topic: A05a/A05b/A07 sequencing; VISION Lifecycle & Sequence Manager

functional.statement: WHEN a user replaces, appends, or deletes a leaf, the system SHALL require and persist a valid reference to a prior leaf that exists in the current or a prior sequence, preventing any dangling cross-reference in the emitted backbone.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a replace operation WHEN no valid prior leaf is referenced THEN the system blocks the operation and flags a dangling-reference defect
GIVEN a delete operation on a leaf originally added as 'new' WHEN applied THEN the backbone points to the correct prior leaf ID
GIVEN all operations across sequences WHEN backbone is emitted THEN no leaf operation references a non-existent prior leaf
functional.rationale: A replace/append/delete with a dangling reference is a validation Error; correct lifecycle linkage is a core correctness requirement.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH lifecycle topic: leaf operations + prior-leaf reference; VISION Lifecycle & Sequence Manager

functional.statement: The system SHALL reconstruct and display the 'current view' of a dossier — the set of leaves that are live after applying all new/replace/append/delete operations across all sequences — and SHALL use it to validate that delete/replace targets exist.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN multiple sequences with lifecycle operations WHEN the current view is requested THEN only live leaves are shown with their originating sequence
GIVEN a replaced leaf WHEN current view renders THEN the superseded leaf is excluded from the live set but retained in history
GIVEN a delete targeting a leaf not in the current view WHEN validated THEN the system raises a defect
functional.rationale: Visual current-view reconstruction eliminates the fragile, rework-prone multi-sequence tracking that plagues incumbent tools.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH lifecycle topic: current-view reconstruction; VISION Lifecycle clarity differentiator

functional.statement: The system SHALL support file reuse, allowing a later sequence to re-point to an unchanged physical file from an earlier sequence rather than re-shipping the bytes, while preserving correct checksums and references.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an unchanged document WHEN a new sequence reuses it THEN the backbone re-points to the prior physical file without duplicating bytes
GIVEN a reused file WHEN packaged THEN the recorded checksum still matches the referenced file
GIVEN a reused file later replaced WHEN validated THEN the replace correctly references the reused leaf
functional.rationale: File reuse reduces package size and matches eCTD lifecycle semantics; helps stay under transmission ceilings.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH lifecycle topic: file reuse; VISION Lifecycle & Sequence Manager

functional.statement: The system SHALL enforce file/folder naming and path hygiene before packaging: lowercase a-z, digits and hyphens only, no spaces or accented/non-ASCII characters, no reserved Windows names, unique leaf IDs, and total path length within 200 characters from the sequence root (mirroring B08, B32, B47/B48).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a filename with spaces or non-ASCII characters WHEN validated THEN the system raises a naming Error and proposes a compliant name
GIVEN a leaf path exceeding 200 characters WHEN validated THEN the system raises a blocking Error mirroring B08
GIVEN duplicate leaf titles in Modules 2-5 or duplicate leaf IDs WHEN validated THEN the system raises the corresponding defect
functional.rationale: Path-length overflow and naming/leaf-ID violations are common rejection triggers (B08/B32/B47/B48).
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic: naming rules, B08, B32, B47/B48; VISION Pre-Submission Validation Report

functional.statement: The system SHALL block packaging of any sequence that contains an empty folder (mirroring A01).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a sequence containing an empty module/sub folder WHEN validated THEN the system raises a blocking Error mirroring A01
GIVEN all folders contain at least one leaf or required file WHEN validated THEN the empty-folder check passes
GIVEN an empty folder defect WHEN displayed THEN it is mapped to the exact folder path
functional.rationale: Empty folders (A01) are a frequent rejection trigger and must be caught before transmission.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic A01; VISION Pre-Submission Validation Report

functional.statement: The system SHALL run a versioned validation-rules engine (default v5.3, effective 2025-05-31; active version selectable) that models each rule as {rule_id, category, severity, description, ruleset_version} across the General/PDF/Referenced/XML/ICH-Backbone/Regional/STF/REP categories using HC's two-tier Error/Warning severity model, blocking on any Error and surfacing Warnings non-blocking.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN the active ruleset is v5.3 WHEN validation runs THEN findings carry rule IDs, category and Error/Warning severity from that version
GIVEN a selectable prior ruleset version WHEN chosen THEN validation evaluates against that version's rules without code changes
GIVEN any Error-severity finding WHEN present THEN transmission is blocked; GIVEN only Warnings THEN transmission is allowed with advisories
functional.rationale: HC updates the ruleset ~annually and uses a two-tier Error/Warning model (not critical/major/minor); a data-driven, versioned engine delivers first-pass-clean by construction. The precise rule count (~90) is approximate; the live spreadsheet is the source of truth.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic: versioned ruleset v5.3, two-tier severity; CORRECTION 'Error/Warning severity model'; CORRECTION '~90 rule count approximate'; VISION continuous validation engine feature

functional.statement: The system SHALL run the validation rules continuously (inline) during authoring, presenting each defect in a severity-colored gutter mapped to the exact file/node with a one-click fix where remediable, rather than only as a terminal gate.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a defect introduced during authoring WHEN it occurs THEN it appears inline mapped to the exact file/node within the editing session
GIVEN a remediable defect WHEN the user clicks the one-click fix THEN the system applies the correction and re-validates
GIVEN Error vs Warning findings WHEN displayed THEN Errors are shown as blocking and Warnings as advisory by color
functional.rationale: Late, terminal validation feedback is the #1 RA pain point; continuous inline validation with one-click fixes is the lead differentiator.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH tool-landscape topic: late validation pain point; VISION continuous validation engine differentiator

functional.statement: The system SHALL produce a downloadable pre-submission validation report that mirrors HC's output — a categorized Error/Warning list with rule IDs against the pinned ruleset version, plus a backbone preview (rendered index.xml and ca-regional.xml, and REP XML rendered via the version-matched HC REP XML stylesheet) with each leaf's MD5 verified against actual bytes.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a built sequence WHEN the report is generated THEN it lists findings grouped by category with rule IDs and Error/Warning severities
GIVEN the report WHEN viewed THEN it renders index.xml and ca-regional.xml previews with per-leaf verified MD5 status and renders REP XML through the version-matched HC stylesheet
GIVEN any unresolved Error WHEN the report is generated THEN it marks the transaction as not transmittable
functional.rationale: Mirroring HC's validation output so nothing reaches CESG that HC will reject is the validation-first thesis; rendering REP XML via HC's own version-matched stylesheet shows what HC will actually display.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD topic; GAP version-matched REP XML stylesheet; VISION Pre-Submission Validation Report

functional.statement: WHEN a transaction is ready to transmit, the system SHALL evaluate the 10 GB per-transaction ceiling pre-flight: packages at or below 10 GB route to the FDA ESG gateway; packages above 10 GB are routed to the physical-media (USB/HDD) workflow with shipping instructions, consistent with HC's guidance that over-limit transactions 'should continue to be submitted on media' (a residual path, not an absolute prohibition).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a 6 GB package WHEN transmission is requested THEN the gateway path is available
GIVEN a 12 GB package WHEN transmission is requested THEN the system routes to the physical-media workflow rather than the gateway
GIVEN the physical-media workflow WHEN selected THEN the system surfaces shipping/media instructions
functional.rationale: 10 GB is the CESG ceiling; over-limit transactions go on physical media. HC phrases this as 'should' (the residual path), so the requirement routes-to-media rather than framing an outright hard prohibition.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH CESG topic: 10 GB ceiling; CORRECTION '10 GB over-limit framing' (route to media, not hard block); VISION Transmission Console

functional.statement: WHEN a package is between 5 GB and 10 GB, the system SHALL offer to schedule transmission after 16:30 EST per Health Canada congestion/overnight-processing guidance.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a 7 GB package WHEN transmission is requested THEN the system offers an after-16:30-EST scheduling option
GIVEN a scheduled send WHEN 16:30 EST is reached THEN the system transmits the queued transaction
GIVEN a sub-5 GB package WHEN transmission is requested THEN no after-16:30 scheduling prompt is required
functional.rationale: HC recommends sending 5-10 GB transactions after 16:30 EST so they process and deliver overnight.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH CESG topic: after-16:30-EST guidance; VISION Transmission Console

functional.statement: The system SHALL enforce one-transaction-at-a-time transmission per dossier, queueing any subsequent sequence until the Health Canada acknowledgement for the prior sequence has been received, per HC's CESG FAQ ('sponsors should ensure they have received the Health Canada acknowledgement for one transaction prior to sending a subsequent transaction'; out-of-order arrival triggers A07).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a sequence transmitted and awaiting acknowledgement WHEN the next sequence is queued THEN the system holds it until the prior acknowledgement arrives
GIVEN the prior sequence's HC acknowledgement is received WHEN the queue is processed THEN the next sequence becomes eligible to send
GIVEN two sequences for different dossiers WHEN transmitted THEN per-dossier serialization does not block the unrelated dossier
functional.rationale: The CESG FAQ confirms sponsors should receive the HC acknowledgement for one transaction before sending the next sequence for the same dossier; out-of-order arrival causes A07.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH/CORRECTION 'REQ-027 sourcing' (confirmed against live CESG FAQ); VISION Transmission Console

functional.statement: The system SHALL maintain an acknowledgement state machine (SENT -> MDN_RECEIVED -> FDA_ACK -> HC_ACK_RECEIPT) modeling HC's three actual artifacts under FDA ESG NextGen — (1) MDN (AS2/transport receipt; under NextGen this IS ACK1 for AS2), (2) FDA Acknowledgement (ESG accepted/transmitted-to-Center, carries Message ID + Core ID), (3) Health Canada Acknowledgement Receipt (carries the Core ID = true HC delivery) — and SHALL display a transaction as 'received by Health Canada' only upon the Health Canada Acknowledgement Receipt, never on the MDN alone, capturing the Core ID.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a transmitted transaction WHEN only the MDN is received THEN the UI shows transport receipt but not 'received by Health Canada'
GIVEN the FDA Acknowledgement is received WHEN displayed THEN the state advances to FDA_ACK (labelled 'FDA Acknowledgement', not 'ACK1') and the Message ID/Core ID are captured
GIVEN the Health Canada Acknowledgement Receipt is received WHEN displayed THEN the transaction is marked received by Health Canada and the Core ID is stored as the correlation key
functional.rationale: Treating the MDN as success is a real correctness trap; only the HC Acknowledgement Receipt is true delivery. The 'MDN != ACK1' framing conflated two numbering schemes — under NextGen the MDN is ACK1 for AS2; model HC's three artifacts and capture the Core ID.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH CESG topic; CORRECTION 'acknowledgement-chain labeling'; GAP capture/store Core ID; VISION acknowledgement state machine feature

functional.statement: WHEN a transaction is rejected, the system SHALL ingest the emailed eCTD Validation Report PDF, correlate it to the originating transaction via the Core ID, and map each reported error back to the exact file/node in the dossier tree for correction in the next sequence.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a rejection validation report PDF WHEN ingested THEN each listed error is parsed with its rule ID and correlated to the transaction by Core ID
GIVEN parsed errors WHEN displayed THEN each maps to the corresponding file/node in the tree
GIVEN a corrected next sequence WHEN built THEN the previously reported errors are re-validated as resolved
functional.rationale: Ingesting the emailed validation report and mapping it back to the tree closes the rejection feedback loop; the Core ID is the stable correlation key.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH lifecycle topic; GAP Core ID correlation key; VISION acknowledgement state machine feature

functional.statement: The system SHALL model the post-receipt DSTS lifecycle as a state machine: Processing (~10 days) -> Screening (45-day target, with SAL/SDN/SRL outcomes) -> Review (ANDS 180-day target) -> decision (NOC/NOD/NON), deriving the NOD/NON Inactive window (Inactive-45 vs Inactive-90) from submission/application type rather than hardcoding 45, and reflecting Inactive statuses accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a transaction received by HC WHEN tracking starts THEN the status begins at Processing and advances through the modelled phases
GIVEN an SDN is recorded at screening WHEN the status updates THEN it transitions to Inactive-45
GIVEN a NOD/NON WHEN issued THEN the Inactive window (Inactive-45 or Inactive-90) is derived from the submission/application type, not hardcoded
GIVEN a decision is recorded WHEN entered THEN the status reflects NOC, NOD, or NON
functional.rationale: Modelling the DSTS lifecycle turns the portal from a publisher into a submission-lifecycle system. HC sets Inactive-45 or Inactive-90 on NOD/NON depending on submission type, so the window must be type-derived.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH lifecycle topic: DSTS statuses; CORRECTION 'Inactive-45/90 hardcoding'; VISION Lifecycle / DSTS Status Tracker

functional.statement: The system SHALL run deadline timers with proactive reminders for screening and review deficiencies — SDN 45 days, clarifax tiers in the 2-15 calendar-day range (default by performance-standard tier but adjustable per HC-agreed window per notice), NOD 90 days (45 days for DIN) — and SHALL implement clock-stop logic that pauses the review clock during sponsor response windows.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an SDN dated today WHEN the timer starts THEN a 45-day countdown with reminders is created

GIVEN a clarifax under the 180-300 day standard WHEN issued THEN a default 15-day response window is set (default 5-day under the 0-90 day standard), and the window is overridable to the HC-agreed value (e.g. 2 days for clinical-trial screening clarifax, 5 days for multi-clarifax Division 1 changes)
GIVEN a NOD for an ANDS WHEN issued THEN a 90-day timer starts and the review clock is paused until response
functional.rationale: Deadline misses auto-convert to withdrawal; timers and clock-stops materially de-risk filings. HC states the 2-15 day clarifax tiers are guidelines that can be adjusted longer or shorter, so they must be overridable defaults, not hardcoded.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH fees/standards topic; CORRECTION 'clarifax windows adjustable'; VISION DSTS deadline engine feature

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide a Q&A-format response-sequence builder that attaches the original notice (SDN/clarifax/NOD/NON), authors answers referencing the applicable submission sections, and files the response as a new eCTD sequence in the same format as the original.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an original notice WHEN a response is started THEN the builder attaches a copy of the notice to the new sequence
GIVEN a Q&A response WHEN authored THEN each answer references the applicable submission section
GIVEN a completed response WHEN filed THEN it becomes the next valid eCTD sequence in the same format
functional.rationale: Deficiency responses must be filed as new eCTD sequences in Q&A format including the original notice.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH lifecycle topic: Q&A response sequence; VISION DSTS Status Tracker

functional.statement: The system SHALL support withdrawal (explicit and auto-interpreted on deadline lapse or deficient/unsolicited response), refiling without prejudice, and request-for-reconsideration paths, producing the corresponding hyphenated W status (NOD-W, NON-W) using HC's exact acronyms.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an SDN/NOD/NON response window that lapses WHEN the deadline passes THEN the system records an auto-interpreted withdrawal with the hyphenated W status (NOD-W / NON-W)
GIVEN a withdrawn submission WHEN the sponsor refiles THEN the system allows refiling without blocking the dossier
GIVEN an NON-W WHEN the sponsor requests reconsideration THEN the system supports the reconsideration path
functional.rationale: HC auto-interprets deadline lapses as withdrawal; HC's exact acronyms are NOD-W and NON-W (hyphenated), so controlled-vocabulary labels must match.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH lifecycle topic; CORRECTION 'W-status notation' (NOD-W/NON-W hyphen); VISION DSTS Status Tracker

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide a portfolio dashboard showing every dossier's current phase, days-elapsed versus the applicable service standard, and at-risk flags, measuring an ANDS (Division 1 & 8 NDS/ANDS/SNDS/SANDS) against HC's 100% on-time-to-first-decision commitment, and applying the 90% on-time standard only to other classes it also tracks (Notifiable Changes, CTAs).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN multiple dossiers WHEN the dashboard loads THEN each shows phase, days elapsed, and target for its submission class
GIVEN an ANDS WHEN on-time performance is evaluated THEN it is measured against the 100% on-time commitment, not 90%
GIVEN a Notifiable Change or CTA also tracked WHEN evaluated THEN the 90% on-time standard is applied to it
GIVEN a dossier approaching its service-standard target WHEN evaluated THEN it is flagged at-risk
functional.rationale: For Division 1 & 8 drug submissions HC's published target is 100% to first decision; 90% applies to other classes. Measuring an ANDS against 90% understates the commitment.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH fees/standards topic; CORRECTION 'on-time KPI' (ANDS=100%, 90% for NC/CTA); VISION Portfolio Dashboard

functional.statement: The system SHALL resolve an ANDS to its Schedule 1 fee grouping (typically 'Comparative studies'), compute the current fiscal-year amount via a per-grouping escalation table keyed by April-1 effective date — applying a CPI escalation (Fee = A + (A x B)) to most groupings but a fixed 2% ministerial-authority escalation to the subset that uses it (DMF, Certificate of Pharmaceutical Product, Certificate of Supplemental Protection, Human Drug Dealer's Licence) — and display the grouping rationale, amount, and applicable fiscal year. The ANDS comparative-studies seed values SHALL be $70,750 (FY2025-26, eff. Apr 1 2025) and $71,953 (FY2026-27), with $53,836 treated as a historical CPI-anchor seed only (never shown as current).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an ANDS relying on comparative studies WHEN the fee is resolved THEN the grouping is 'Comparative studies' with its rationale and the FY2025-26 amount $70,750 (or FY2026-27 $71,953) shown — never $53,836 as current

GIVEN a submission-date fiscal year WHEN the fee is computed THEN the system applies the correct per-grouping escalation basis (CPI Fee=A+(AxB) for most, fixed 2% for the ministerial-authority subset)
GIVEN an updated annual fee table WHEN loaded THEN amounts and per-grouping escalation bases update without code changes
functional.rationale: $53,836 is the FY2020-21 base (~24% low); the current ANDS comparative-studies fee is $70,750/$71,953. Escalation is not a single global CPI rate — a defined subset escalates at a fixed 2% ministerial rate, so the table must be keyed per grouping with a per-grouping basis.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH fees topic; CORRECTION 'stale seed fee amounts'; CORRECTION 'CPI escalation basis' (2% vs CPI split); VISION Fee/Service-Standard View

functional.statement: The system SHALL track fee mitigation eligibility — 100% small-business first-submission remission, 50% subsequent-ANDS remission (gated on an affiliation/financial attestation upload), and deferral-until-NOC — along with invoice status per sponsor and per submission.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a small business's first-ever drug submission WHEN mitigation is evaluated THEN 100% remission eligibility is offered
GIVEN a subsequent ANDS WHEN 50% remission is claimed THEN the system requires the affiliation/financial attestation upload
GIVEN a concurrent authorization application WHEN deferral is selected THEN payment is deferred until NOC and invoice status reflects deferral
functional.rationale: Mitigation and deferral are statutory (SOR/2019-124) and give sponsors fee transparency; attestation gating prevents improper remission.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH fees topic: remission/deferral; VISION Fee/Service-Standard View

functional.statement: The system SHALL track the per-DIN annual Right-to-Sell fee separately from one-time submission fees, keying the amount by drug type (prescription ~$5,531 / non-prescription ~$3,334 / disinfectant ~$1,730 FY2025-26; ~$5,626 / ~$3,391 / ~$1,760 FY2026-27; biocide $1,535 base) and pinning the statutory due date of October 1, with outstanding-balance flags per DIN.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an authorized DIN of a given drug type WHEN the annual fee is tracked THEN the system records its type-specific amount and the October 1 statutory due date
GIVEN an approaching October 1 due date WHEN evaluated THEN the system schedules a reminder
GIVEN an unpaid annual fee WHEN reviewed THEN the DIN shows an outstanding-balance flag
functional.rationale: The recurring per-DIN annual fee is distinct from submission-examination fees, varies by drug type, and is due October 1 — both the type differentiation and the statutory due date were previously omitted.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH fees topic; CORRECTION 'annual right-to-sell fee modeling' (by drug type + Oct 1 due date); VISION Fee/Service-Standard View

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide multi-tenant role-based access control scoped to the sponsor organization, with least-privilege roles (org admin, regulatory author, QA reviewer/signer, regulatory operations/publisher, read-only) and hard tenant isolation so one sponsor org cannot access another's dossiers or data.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a user in sponsor org A WHEN they attempt to access org B's dossier THEN access is denied and the attempt is audit-logged
GIVEN a read-only user WHEN they attempt to author or transmit THEN the action is blocked
GIVEN role assignments WHEN configured THEN each role grants only its least-privilege capabilities, including per-dossier authorization
functional.rationale: Multi-tenant isolation and least-privilege RBAC are required to legally hold per-sponsor submission/health data.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH compliance topic: RBAC + tenant isolation; VISION Sponsor Org Admin persona

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide an approval gate where a QA reviewer performs a documented audit-trail review and an authorized signer applies an electronic signature before transmission becomes available for a transaction, and SHALL anchor the e-signature handling to the HPFB Electronic Signatures Policy (case-by-case HC acceptance). The Annex-11/ALCOA+ control set is implemented as a VALUE-ADD best practice, not as a Health Canada mandate.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an unsigned transaction WHEN transmission is attempted THEN the system blocks it pending QA review and signature
GIVEN a QA audit-trail review WHEN completed THEN the named reviewer's sign-off is recorded
GIVEN the required e-signature is applied WHEN the gate evaluates THEN transmission becomes available

GIVEN the e-signature approach WHEN configured THEN the requirement notes HC accepts e-signatures case-by-case under the HPFB Electronic Signatures Policy (a permission, not a mandated Part-11/Annex-11 control set)
functional.rationale: HC accepts e-signatures on submission content case-by-case under the HPFB Electronic Signatures Policy; Annex-11/ALCOA+ apply to GMP/GxP source records and inspected establishments, not to a sponsor's eCTD assembly tool. The QA/sign-off gate is retained as a value-add control, honestly framed.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH compliance topic; CORRECTION 'ALCOA+/Annex-11 e-signature framed as HC mandate'; GAP anchor to HPFB Electronic Signatures Policy; VISION sign-off gate

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide a manageable controlled-vocabulary and reference-data layer that is updatable as data without code changes, version-pinning each artifact independently: validation ruleset versions, the CA Module 1 Schema version (v2.2 XSD, 2012-07-06), the ICH eCTD DTD version (3.2.2), HC-published Module 1 controlled-vocabulary/enumeration files keyed to the schema version, fee groupings/CPI-and-2% escalation tables by fiscal year, service standards, the Module 1 placement table (2024-04-02), REP template versions (CO v5.0.0, RT v5.1.0, PI 2024-02-12) and the version-matched REP XML stylesheet, and the management-of-drug-submissions guidance edition (2025-10-01).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN HC publishes a new annual fee/standard notice WHEN the reference data is updated THEN the new values apply without redeploying code
GIVEN a new validation ruleset, Module 1 schema (v2.2), or ICH DTD (3.2.2) version WHEN added THEN each is independently selectable/pinned without code changes
GIVEN HC's published CV/enumeration files WHEN ingested THEN the portal uses them (not a hand-maintained list) and rejects out-of-vocabulary values per I08/H08
GIVEN an updated Module 1 placement table or management-of-drug-submissions guidance edition (2025-10-01) WHEN loaded THEN tree placement and day-counts reflect it
functional.rationale: HC artifacts change ~annually and the Module 1 schema/DTD can rev independently of the validation ruleset; CVs must come from HC's published files; the management guidance was re-issued 2025-10-01. Data-driven, independently pinned reference data keeps the portal current without releases.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH multiple topics; GAP schema v2.2 + DTD 3.2.2 as version-pinned data; GAP HC-published CV files; GAP REP XML stylesheet; CORRECTION 'guidance edition not pinned' (2025-10-01); CORRECTION 'REP template versions stale'; VISION reference-data layer

functional.statement: The system SHALL be architected with the backbone generator behind a version-pluggable interface, assigning persistent document UUIDs now, so the same content model can emit eCTD v3.2.2 today and the HL7-RPS eCTD v4.0 message (UUIDs, Genericode controlled vocabularies, Context of Use, two-way messaging) when adopted. v4.0 adoption dates are industry-roadmap ESTIMATES, not HC-fixed commitments (the HC draft CA Module 1 TIG went to consultation in June 2019 and its original timeline has lapsed).
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a content model WHEN exported THEN the v3.2.2 ICH+CA backbone is produced through the generator interface
GIVEN a document WHEN created THEN it is assigned a persistent UUID retained across sequences and applications
GIVEN a future v4.0 generator implementation WHEN selected THEN the same content model emits an HL7-RPS message without re-authoring content
GIVEN v4.0 readiness work WHEN scoped THEN any voluntary/mandatory dates are labelled as industry estimates, not HC-published deadlines
functional.rationale: A pluggable backbone and persistent UUIDs avoid a re-platform. The voluntary/mandatory v4.0 dates are industry-roadmap estimates with no binding HC notice as of 2026-06, so they must not be presented as HC-fixed.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH eCTD/tool topics; CORRECTION 'v4.0 timeline framing' (industry estimates); VISION eCTD v4.0 readiness feature

functional.statement: WHEN identifier values are entered, the system SHALL validate their formats at input: Company ID as an HC-assigned opaque token (loose validation; NOT hardcoded as 5 numeric digits), drug Dossier ID matching a prefix-by-type pattern (default 'e', ^[a-z][0-9]{6,7}$), sequence folders matching ^[0-9]{4}$, and DINs 8 digits, and SHALL bind each transaction's backbone metadata to the registered Dossier ID and REP values.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a Company ID WHEN entered THEN the system accepts HC's opaque-token format (alphanumeric, e.g. K18276) and does NOT reject non-5-digit values
GIVEN a drug Dossier ID WHEN entered THEN it is validated against the prefix-by-type 6-or-7-digit pattern (default 'e')
GIVEN backbone metadata WHEN it does not match the registered Dossier ID/REP values THEN the system blocks export
GIVEN an 8-digit DIN field WHEN a non-8-digit value is entered THEN the system rejects it
functional.rationale: Unregistered or mismatched identifiers cause rejection. The Company ID is an HC-assigned opaque token (a 5-digit-numeric validator would reject HC's own IDs), and drug Dossier IDs use 'e' with 6 or 7 digits, not '^m[0-9]{6}$'.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH REP topic; CORRECTION 'Dossier ID format'; CORRECTION 'Company ID format too strict'; VISION single-entry metadata differentiator

functional.statement: The system SHALL enter REP CO/RT/PI identifiers once and flow them into both the REP XML and the eCTD ca-regional.xml backbone metadata, and SHALL auto-populate the Dossier ID into the sponsor-authored cover letter generated from the portal's OWN template, without re-keying.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN identifiers captured in the CO/RT templates WHEN a transaction is assembled THEN the same values populate the ca-regional.xml metadata
GIVEN a Dossier ID WHEN the portal generates a cover letter from its own template THEN the Dossier ID is auto-populated (no HC cover-letter form is used)
GIVEN a change to a captured identifier WHEN saved THEN both the REP XML and backbone metadata reflect the change
functional.rationale: Unified single-entry metadata kills re-keying. The cover letter is sponsor-authored from the portal's own template (HC provides only the slot), so the requirement must not imply an HC fillable cover-letter form.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH tool topic; CORRECTION 'cover letter wrongly implied an HC fillable template'; VISION unified single-entry metadata differentiator

functional.statement: The system SHALL maintain a per-section required-document checklist for the configured ANDS content model and SHALL prevent a transaction from passing the validation gate while mandatory documents (including the QOS-CE for Module 2.3, the CS-BE electronic copy in Module 1.6, and required .docx-alongside-PDF where specified) are missing; the cover-letter slot is satisfied by the portal-generated sponsor-authored cover letter.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN the ANDS content model WHEN the checklist renders THEN each required section lists its mandatory documents, including 2.3 QOS-CE and the 1.6 CS-BE copy
GIVEN a missing mandatory document WHEN the gate is evaluated THEN the system blocks with a missing-content finding mapped to the section
GIVEN a section requiring a .docx alongside a PDF WHEN only the PDF is present THEN the checklist flags the missing .docx
functional.rationale: Missing-content rejections are prevented by enforcing the ANDS-specific required-document checklist; the cover-letter expectation is the portal-generated sponsor document, not an HC form.
functional.traces_to: RESEARCH ANDS topic; CORRECTION 'cover letter'; GAP QOS-CE; VISION Dossier Workspace required-document checklist

functional.statement: WHEN a generated REP CO/RT/PI XML or backbone fails HC schema/DTD validation or an external HC/FDA service (FDA ESG, REP ID return) is unavailable, the system SHALL surface the specific schema-validation error or service-outage condition, retain the in-progress work without data loss, and provide a guided retry/resume path rather than silently failing or discarding state.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an FDA ESG gateway timeout or 5xx during transmission WHEN it occurs THEN the system records the failure, keeps the packaged sequence intact and un-consumed, and offers a retry without forcing a re-package
GIVEN a REP XML that fails Canadian Module 1 Schema v2.2 validation WHEN generation runs THEN the system reports the exact failing element/line and does not emit a 'final-' file

GIVEN an interrupted transmission (network drop mid-send) WHEN connectivity returns THEN the system resolves whether the transaction was received (via ack/Core-ID reconciliation) before allowing a duplicate send
functional.rationale: Real submissions hit timeouts, 5xx, and schema failures; silent failure or duplicate transmission is itself a rejection/integrity risk.
functional.traces_to: GAP: validation-failure and external-service-outage handling absent from REQ-003/REQ-014/REQ-025/REQ-028

functional.statement: WHEN a transmission attempt does not complete cleanly (no MDN within a configured window, MDN received but no FDA Acknowledgement, or an FDA Acknowledgement indicating a transport-level rejection), the system SHALL detect the stalled/failed state via timeout monitors, alert the responsible operator, and prevent an unverified duplicate transmission of the same sequence to the same dossier, correlating states by Message ID/Core ID against FDA ESG NextGen.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a SENT transaction with no MDN after the configured timeout WHEN the monitor fires THEN the transaction is flagged 'transport unconfirmed' and the operator is alerted
GIVEN an MDN received but no FDA Acknowledgement within the configured window WHEN the monitor fires THEN the transaction is flagged for investigation and not auto-marked received

GIVEN an operator attempting to resend a sequence whose delivery state is unresolved WHEN resend is requested THEN the system requires explicit confirmation and records the duplicate-send rationale in the audit trail
functional.rationale: The ack state machine models success states but not stalls, transport rejections, or duplicate-send protection; correlation must use the NextGen Message ID/Core ID.
functional.traces_to: GAP: ack-chain timeout/failure handling absent from REQ-028; CORRECTION 'FDA ESG NextGen' (relabel FDA Acknowledgement, Core ID)

functional.statement: The system SHALL model a multi-dossier / multi-product portfolio in which a single sponsor org holds many dossiers and a single product family may span multiple DINs, strengths, and dossiers, and SHALL prevent cross-dossier contamination of sequences, identifiers, lifecycle operations, and prior-leaf references.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a sponsor with multiple dossiers WHEN a sequence is created THEN its 4-digit numbering, lifecycle operations, and prior-leaf references are scoped strictly to its own dossier
GIVEN a multi-strength product family WHEN dossiers are organized THEN the system represents the product-to-DIN-to-dossier relationships without forcing them into a single sequence stream
GIVEN a prior-leaf reference WHEN authored THEN it can only resolve to a leaf within the same dossier and never to another dossier's sequence
functional.rationale: The portal must hold a realistic multi-product portfolio; cross-dossier reference or numbering leakage would corrupt backbones and is a top audit concern.
functional.traces_to: GAP: explicit multi-dossier/multi-product/multi-DIN modeling and isolation absent

functional.statement: WHEN a sponsor needs to file an administrative or corrective sequence (e.g., a sequence that reorganizes, withdraws, or corrects a prior transaction's lifecycle without changing scientific content), the system SHALL support administrative-type regulatory activities and corrective/reorganization sequences that file as a valid next eCTD sequence with correct lifecycle operations and no scientific re-review trigger where not warranted.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a need to withdraw a single leaf erroneously filed WHEN a corrective sequence is built THEN the system files a delete operation referencing the correct prior leaf as the next sequence number
GIVEN an administrative regulatory activity type WHEN selected THEN the RT template and content model reflect the administrative subset, not a full ANDS content set
GIVEN a reorganization sequence WHEN assembled THEN the current-view reconstruction remains consistent and no dangling references are introduced
functional.rationale: Real dossiers require administrative and corrective sequences beyond content and deficiency-response sequences.
functional.traces_to: GAP: administrative/corrective/reorganization sequence types beyond REQ-032

functional.statement: WHEN a sponsor must transfer ownership of a dossier/DIN to another company, change the company name, or merge/acquire another sponsor org, the system SHALL support a dossier/manufacturer transfer-of-ownership workflow that updates REP Company ID and contact records, preserves the full prior sequence history and audit trail, and files the appropriate administrative sequence.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a transfer of ownership WHEN executed THEN the dossier's full sequence history and audit trail are preserved and re-associated to the receiving org without rewriting prior sequences
GIVEN a company name change WHEN recorded THEN a new CO transaction is generated while prior Company ID linkage and history remain intact
GIVEN a transfer WHEN completed THEN tenant access is re-scoped so only the new owner org can access the dossier and the change is audit-logged with actor and timestamp
functional.rationale: Manufacturer transfers, name changes, and M&A are routine over a product lifecycle and touch REP identifiers, tenant isolation, and history preservation.
functional.traces_to: GAP: transfer-of-ownership / company name change / org merge lifecycle absent

functional.statement: WHEN a screening or review deficiency response is received from the sponsor that is incomplete, late, or itself deficient, the system SHALL distinguish among acceptable, deficient, and unsolicited responses, track the resulting HC outcome (e.g., acceptance, further clarifax, conversion to withdrawal), and prevent filing a response after the applicable window has closed without an explicit override and rationale.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a clarifax response prepared after its (default 2-15 day) window has elapsed WHEN filing is attempted THEN the system warns the window has closed and requires an explicit override with recorded rationale
GIVEN a response HC deems deficient WHEN the outcome is recorded THEN the system advances the dossier state accordingly (e.g., to withdrawal interpretation) and timestamps it
GIVEN an unsolicited submission of additional data during review WHEN filed THEN the system tags it as unsolicited and records the regulatory risk advisory
functional.rationale: REQ-031/032/033 cover issuing timers and building responses but not the response-quality/late-response branch that triggers withdrawal or further clarifax.
functional.traces_to: GAP: deficient/late/unsolicited response handling beyond REQ-031/032/033

functional.statement: The system SHALL track multiple concurrent deficiency notices (e.g., overlapping clarifax requests, simultaneous screening and review queries) per dossier with independent clocks and clock-stops, and SHALL correctly recompute the review service-standard clock when overlapping sponsor response windows pause and resume it, using the per-notice adjustable (2-15 day) windows.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN two clarifax requests open simultaneously WHEN clocks run THEN each maintains its own (adjustable) response deadline and reminder schedule independently
GIVEN overlapping response windows WHEN the review clock-stop is computed THEN the system pauses the 180-day review clock for the union of active response windows and resumes correctly
GIVEN a closed clarifax while another remains open WHEN recomputed THEN the review clock reflects the still-paused state
functional.rationale: Real reviews have multiple overlapping clarifax cycles; a single clock-stop model miscomputes the service standard when windows overlap. The clarifax windows are adjustable guidelines, not fixed.
functional.traces_to: GAP: concurrent/overlapping deficiency clocks and union clock-stop logic absent from REQ-031; CORRECTION 'clarifax windows adjustable'

functional.statement: The system SHALL compute and display the applicable regulatory deadlines using Health Canada's calendar conventions — calendar vs business days as specified per notice type, Canadian federal statutory holidays, and the configured review timezone — and SHALL not silently roll a deadline that lands on a weekend or holiday without surfacing the adjusted due date.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a clarifax window WHEN the nominal due date falls on a Canadian statutory holiday THEN the system shows the adjusted due date per HC convention and flags the adjustment
GIVEN a deadline computation WHEN calendar-day vs business-day basis differs by notice type THEN the system applies the correct basis for that notice type
GIVEN a holiday calendar update WHEN loaded as reference data THEN deadline computations reflect it without code changes
functional.rationale: Deadline misses auto-convert to withdrawal, so the exact day-counting basis, holidays, and timezone are material.
functional.traces_to: GAP: holiday/business-day/timezone-aware deadline computation absent from REQ-031/NFR-013

functional.statement: The system SHALL bind every applied electronic signature to an immutable signature manifest that records the exact artifact (sequence/leaf/backbone) and its checksum at signing time, the signer identity and authentication method, the signing timestamp with timezone, and the signature meaning, and SHALL detect and flag any post-signature modification of the signed content before transmission. This manifest is implemented as a VALUE-ADD integrity control (it operationalizes the HPFB case-by-case e-signature policy), not as an HC-mandated Annex-11 control.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a transaction signed by an authorized signer WHEN the manifest is written THEN it records the signed artifact identifiers, their checksums at signing, signer identity, auth method, timestamp+timezone, and meaning
GIVEN content modified after signature WHEN the gate re-evaluates THEN the system invalidates the signature, flags the broken manifest, and re-blocks transmission
GIVEN a signed package WHEN exported THEN the signature manifest is retained and exportable as part of the audit record
functional.rationale: An auditor demands proof that the signed bytes are the transmitted bytes; this tamper-evident manifest is a value-add integrity control consistent with the HPFB case-by-case e-signature policy, not an HC Annex-11 mandate.
functional.traces_to: GAP: e-signature manifest binding + post-sign tamper detection; CORRECTION 'ALCOA+/Annex-11 framed as HC mandate' (value-add framing)

functional.statement: The system SHALL enforce configurable data-retention and legal-hold policies on submission content, sequences, acknowledgements, audit trails, and signature manifests that meet or exceed the genuine PIPEDA breach-record minimum (>=24 months) and any sponsor-contracted/provincial retention periods, prevent deletion of records under legal hold or within the retention window, and log any disposition event. Retention beyond the PIPEDA breach-record minimum is a configurable VALUE-ADD/contractual control, not a fixed HC mandate.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a record within its mandated retention window WHEN deletion is attempted THEN the system blocks it and records the blocked attempt
GIVEN a legal hold placed on a dossier WHEN any disposition is attempted THEN the system prevents it until the hold is released by an authorized role
GIVEN a record past retention with no hold WHEN disposition runs THEN the event is logged with actor, timestamp, and records affected
functional.rationale: PIPEDA mandates a >=24-month breach-record retention; broader submission-record retention and legal hold are standard audit/contractual demands implemented as configurable value-add, honestly distinguished from the genuine PIPEDA minimum.
functional.traces_to: GAP: retention schedule + legal hold + disposition logging absent; CORRECTION 'basis' distinction (PIPEDA vs value-add)

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide disaster-recovery and business-continuity capabilities for all dossier content, sequences, acknowledgements, audit trails, and signature manifests, including defined recovery point and recovery time objectives and periodic tested restoration; where a sponsor/contract/provincial-law requires in-Canada residency, backups SHALL be pinned to in-Canada regions. In-Canada/Protected B residency is a configurable VALUE-ADD control, not an HC mandate for a sponsor's submission-prep tool.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a regional failure WHEN recovery is invoked THEN the system restores all dossier content, sequences, acks, audit trails, and signatures to within the defined RPO/RTO
GIVEN a tenant configured for in-Canada residency WHEN backups are created THEN they remain pinned to the configured in-Canada region and are encrypted at rest
GIVEN a scheduled DR test WHEN executed THEN a documented restoration is performed and verified against integrity checksums
functional.rationale: RPO/RTO, tested restoration, and DR are standard regulated-SaaS demands; residency pinning is a configurable value-add driven by the sponsor's own contracts/provincial law, not an HC mandate.
functional.traces_to: GAP: DR/BCP with RPO/RTO, tested restore beyond NFR-010; CORRECTION 'Protected B / residency framing' (value-add)

functional.statement: WHEN HC's eCTD validation ruleset, Module 1 placement table, controlled vocabularies, schema/DTD versions, REP template versions, or management-of-drug-submissions guidance edition change while sequences are in flight, the system SHALL pin each transaction to the versions effective at its build/transmit time, prevent retroactive invalidation of already-accepted sequences, and warn when an in-progress dossier spans a version-effective-date boundary.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a sequence built under ruleset v5.3 WHEN a later ruleset becomes active THEN the accepted sequence's recorded validation result remains pinned to v5.3 and is not retroactively failed
GIVEN an in-progress draft WHEN a new ruleset/schema/guidance effective date passes before transmission THEN the system warns and offers re-validation against the now-active version
GIVEN a schema version change WHEN a dossier's prior sequences used the older schema THEN the current-view and lifecycle references remain valid across the version boundary
functional.rationale: Long-running dossiers cross effective-date boundaries; version-transition pinning prevents retroactive failures and applies equally to schema/DTD, REP templates, and the 2025-10-01 management guidance edition.
functional.traces_to: GAP: ruleset/schema version-transition pinning beyond REQ-022/REQ-040; CORRECTION 'guidance edition' pinning

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide a concurrency/locking model for multi-user authoring of the same dossier and sequence that prevents conflicting simultaneous edits to leaves, metadata, lifecycle operations, and sequence numbering, and SHALL serialize sequence-number assignment so two users cannot both claim the same next 4-digit sequence.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN two users editing the same leaf concurrently WHEN both save THEN the system prevents a lost update via locking or conflict detection and surfaces the conflict
GIVEN two users creating the next sequence for the same dossier simultaneously WHEN they submit THEN exactly one obtains the next number and the other is rejected/retried
GIVEN a held lock WHEN the holder is idle beyond a timeout THEN the lock is safely released without corrupting state
functional.rationale: Concurrent RA users could race the next-sequence assignment or clobber each other's leaf edits; without locking this corrupts the backbone.
functional.traces_to: GAP: multi-user concurrency/locking and serialized sequence assignment absent from REQ-016

functional.statement: WHEN a transaction is routed to the physical-media (>10 GB) workflow, the system SHALL produce a complete media package (the validated eCTD folder tree, backbones, checksums, and a media-manifest/cover documentation), track the physical shipment and its receipt, and reconcile the eventual Health Canada acknowledgement (via Core ID) back to the same transaction record as the gateway path.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a >10 GB transaction WHEN the physical-media workflow runs THEN the system writes the full validated tree plus a media manifest and shipping documentation
GIVEN a shipped media package WHEN tracked THEN the system records carrier/tracking and receipt status against the transaction

GIVEN an HC acknowledgement for a media-shipped transaction WHEN received THEN it reconciles by Core ID to the same dossier/sequence record and advances the DSTS lifecycle identically to gateway transactions
functional.rationale: A real >10 GB workflow must produce the media package, track the shipment, and close the acknowledgement loop using the Core ID correlation key.
functional.traces_to: GAP: physical-media package generation, shipment tracking, and ack reconciliation beyond REQ-025

functional.statement: The system SHALL validate cross-document and metadata consistency across a transaction — DIN/Dossier ID/Company ID agreement among CO/RT/PI, cover letter, and ca-regional.xml; product name, strength, and dosage-form consistency between CRP/PI metadata and content; and STF (Study Tagging File) presence and correctness where Module 5 study data (e.g., BE study reports) requires it — blocking on inconsistencies before packaging.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN identifiers across CO/RT/PI, cover letter, and ca-regional.xml WHEN they disagree THEN the system blocks export and lists the conflicting values
GIVEN product/strength/dosage-form metadata WHEN inconsistent between PI/CRP and content placement THEN the system raises a consistency defect mapped to the source
GIVEN Module 5 study data that requires an STF WHEN the STF is missing or malformed THEN the system raises the corresponding STF-category defect
functional.rationale: Cross-artifact metadata consistency and STF correctness are both real HC validation/rejection triggers.
functional.traces_to: GAP: cross-artifact metadata-consistency and STF validation absent

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide audit-trail export and regulatory-inspection support, producing on demand a complete, human-readable, time-ordered audit record for a given dossier, transaction, or signature — including all state changes, validation results, sign-offs, and transmissions — suitable for Health Canada inspection or third-party audit, without permitting redaction of the underlying immutable trail.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an inspection request for a dossier WHEN export is run THEN the system produces a complete, time-ordered, human-readable audit report covering authoring, validation, sign-off, and transmission events
GIVEN an exported audit report WHEN compared to the live immutable trail THEN no events are omitted or altered
GIVEN an audit export WHEN generated THEN the export action itself is recorded in the audit trail with actor and timestamp
functional.rationale: An HC inspection or audit demands an on-demand, complete, readable export of the immutable trail.
functional.traces_to: GAP: inspection-ready audit export beyond NFR-002 internal trail

functional.statement: The system SHALL generate, fill, and validate the Health Canada Quality Overall Summary — Chemical Entities (QOS-CE) template for Module 2.3 (parallel to the CS-BE handling in REQ-008), and SHALL flag a missing or incomplete QOS-CE as a screening-deficiency risk.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN an ANDS content model WHEN Module 2.3 is assembled THEN the system provides a QOS-CE builder that produces a conformant HC QOS-CE document
GIVEN a completed QOS-CE WHEN validated THEN structural completeness against the HC template is checked
GIVEN a missing or incomplete QOS-CE WHEN the gate is evaluated THEN the system blocks with a screening-deficiency-risk finding mapped to Module 2.3
functional.rationale: Module 3 plus the 2.3 QOS-CE is mandatory for an ANDS; a missing/incorrect QOS is a screening-deficiency risk, and nothing previously made the portal generate/validate the actual QOS-CE template.
functional.traces_to: GAP: QOS-CE template for Module 2.3 (parallel to REQ-008 CS-BE)

functional.statement: The system SHALL detect when Health Canada misses an applicable service standard (per REQ-034: ANDS 100% on-time-to-first-decision; 90% for tracked NC/CTA) and SHALL surface and trigger the statutory 25% fee-credit entitlement (SOR/2019-124) for the affected submission.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a submission whose review exceeds its applicable performance standard WHEN evaluated against days-elapsed-vs-target THEN the system flags the missed standard
GIVEN a missed standard WHEN detected THEN the system surfaces the 25%-of-fee-paid credit entitlement and records it against the submission's fee record
GIVEN a credit entitlement WHEN displayed THEN it shows the 25% amount relative to the fee actually paid
functional.rationale: SOR/2019-124 credits the sponsor 25% of the fee paid if the submission is not reviewed within the performance standard; the portal already tracks days-elapsed-vs-target and the fee, so this concrete sponsor value should be surfaced.
functional.traces_to: GAP: 25% fee credit on missed service standard; CORRECTION 'on-time KPI' (surface 25% fee-credit)

functional.statement: The system SHALL version the bioequivalence acceptance ruleset by submission date and dosage-form class, and branch Cmax validation accordingly: point-estimate (relative mean) within 80.0-125.0% for legacy/pre-ICH-M13A or non-immediate-release products, versus the full 90% confidence interval within 80.00-125.00% under ICH M13A (effective 2025-12-27, immediate-release solid oral). It SHALL NOT hardcode a single Cmax rule.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN a submission date and dosage-form class WHEN the BE ruleset is resolved THEN the system selects the correct Cmax rule (point-estimate vs 90% CI)
GIVEN an IR solid-oral product filed on/after 2025-12-27 WHEN Cmax is validated THEN the full 90% CI must be within 80.00-125.00% (M13A)
GIVEN a legacy or non-IR product WHEN Cmax is validated THEN only the point estimate must be within 80.0-125.0% and no 90% CI is required for Cmax
functional.rationale: ICH M13A is now in force at HC for IR oral generics; a single hardcoded Cmax rule will wrongly fail/accept legacy or non-IR products, so the rule must be versioned by date and dosage-form class.
functional.traces_to: GAP: model ICH M13A transition (version BE ruleset, branch Cmax); CORRECTION 'Cmax acceptance criterion versioned'

functional.statement: The system SHALL provide a dedicated Study Tagging File (STF) generation and validation capability for transactions containing study data, generating conformant STF leaves where Module 5 BE study reports (or any Module 4/5 study data) appear and validating them as their own HC eCTD validation category.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN Module 5 BE study reports WHEN the sequence is assembled THEN the system generates the corresponding STF leaves
GIVEN generated STFs WHEN validated THEN they are checked against the STF validation category rules independently of other categories
GIVEN study data present without a required STF WHEN validated THEN the system raises a blocking STF-category defect
functional.rationale: STF is its own HC eCTD validation category with its own rules; missing/incorrect STFs are a validation finding wherever Module 4/5 study data appears (low-frequency for ANDS but required for Module 5 BE reports).
functional.traces_to: GAP: dedicated STF builder/validator (STF is its own validation category)

functional.statement: The system SHALL bundle and version-track the HC-published REP XML stylesheet package (pharmabio_stylesheets, 2025-09-10) matched to the REP template generation, and SHALL render generated REP XML through that stylesheet for human review before filing.
acceptance_criteria: GIVEN generated REP XML WHEN preview is requested THEN it is rendered via the version-matched HC REP XML stylesheet showing what HC will display
GIVEN a REP template version WHEN selected THEN the matching stylesheet version is used for rendering
GIVEN a stylesheet update from HC WHEN loaded THEN the rendering reflects it without code changes (per REQ-040)
functional.rationale: HC ships XSL stylesheets to render REP XML for human review; without a version-matched stylesheet the portal cannot reliably preview what HC will display, which also supports the REQ-024 preview.
functional.traces_to: GAP: version-matched REP XML stylesheet (supports REQ-024 preview)
